items.question_text: A registrar says surgery will be sooner if he enrols and delayed if he declines. Consent to research is voluntary. Which of the following is most accurate?
options: Coercive. Care must not be conditional on joining the trial
Earlier surgery for enrolment is acceptable
A free drug repairs the link
Public patients can be pressured
Decline means delayed surgery is fine
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

A. Coercive. Care must not be conditional on joining the trial

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
A registrar says surgery will be sooner if he enrols and delayed if he declines. Consent to research is voluntary.

2. THE RULE
Research participation is voluntary: people may decline or withdraw at any time without reason and their clinical care continues unchanged.

3. WHY A IS CORRECT
Care is not a reward for saying yes.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
B. Earlier surgery for enrolment is acceptable: Linking care to enrolment is coercion.
C. A free drug repairs the link: Inducements do not repair coercion.
D. Public patients can be pressured: All patients have the right to refuse.
E. Decline means delayed surgery is fine: Penalising refusal is coercive.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Research participation is voluntary: people may decline or withdraw at any time without reason and their clinical care continues unchanged.

---

EDITED BY HEISENBERG

items.question_text: A woman in a randomised trial wants to withdraw and will not say why. The study coordinator tells her that withdrawing means losing her clinical follow-up. Which of the following is most accurate?
options: She must give a reason, and withdrawal cancels follow-up
She may withdraw without a reason, and clinical care continues
Further research visits can be compelled
A coordinator can refuse withdrawal
Leaving the study ends outpatient care
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

B. She may withdraw without a reason, and clinical care continues

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
A woman in a randomised trial wants to withdraw and will not say why. The study coordinator tells her that withdrawing means losing her clinical follow-up.

2. THE RULE
Research participation is voluntary: people may decline or withdraw at any time without reason and their clinical care continues unchanged.

3. WHY B IS CORRECT
Withdrawal is a right. Care is separate.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. She must give a reason, and withdrawal cancels follow-up: No reason is needed, and care continues.
C. Further research visits can be compelled: Research participation is voluntary.
D. A coordinator can refuse withdrawal: Coordinators cannot refuse withdrawal.
E. Leaving the study ends outpatient care: Clinical care continues.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Research participation is voluntary: people may decline or withdraw at any time without reason and their clinical care continues unchanged.

---

EDITED BY HEISENBERG

items.question_text: The principal investigator owns 30% of the company making the trial device. The consent form does not mention it. Participants are told about interests that could influence the study. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Disclose the ownership in the consent. Do not hide a financial interest
30% can be omitted because it would reduce recruitment
Tell only the ethics committee
Mention it only in the final paper
Move the shares to a spouse and say nothing
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

A. Disclose the ownership in the consent. Do not hide a financial interest

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
The principal investigator owns 30% of the company making the trial device. The consent form does not mention it. Participants are told about interests that could influence the study.

2. THE RULE
Researchers disclose financial conflicts of interest in consent materials and report serious adverse events promptly to the sponsor and ethics committee.

3. WHY A IS CORRECT
Financial interest in the consent. Do not hide it.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
B. 30% can be omitted because it would reduce recruitment: Recruitment concerns do not justify concealment.
C. Tell only the ethics committee: Participants must also be informed.
D. Mention it only in the final paper: Disclosure must happen before consent.
E. Move the shares to a spouse and say nothing: Transferring shares to a spouse still leaves a conflict.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Researchers disclose financial conflicts of interest in consent materials and report serious adverse events promptly to the sponsor and ethics committee.

---

EDITED BY HEISENBERG

items.question_text: One participant dies of a pulmonary embolus a week after the new procedure. The other 40 did well. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Mention the death only if the journal asks
Report the death as a serious adverse event, to the sponsor and the ethics committee, now
A good result in the other 40 patients delays reporting
Reclassify the death without review
Delete the case
items.explanation:
CORRECT ANSWER

B. Report the death as a serious adverse event, to the sponsor and the ethics committee, now

---

1. CLINICAL SITUATION
One participant dies of a pulmonary embolus a week after the new procedure. The other 40 did well.

2. THE RULE
Researchers disclose financial conflicts of interest in consent materials and report serious adverse events promptly to the sponsor and ethics committee.

3. WHY B IS CORRECT
A favourable overall result does not hide a death. Report it.

4. WHY THE OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
A. Mention the death only if the journal asks: SAEs must be reported promptly.
C. A good result in the other 40 patients delays reporting: Good outcomes do not delay SAE reporting.
D. Reclassify the death without review: Causality is assessed through proper review.
E. Delete the case: Deleting data is misconduct.

5. KEY TAKEAWAY
Researchers disclose financial conflicts of interest in consent materials and report serious adverse events promptly to the sponsor and ethics committee.

---
